# s-m-r-t

> s-m-r-t gives an application an explicit, governed model of its meaning, operations, interfaces, and agent access. The application model can project into human interfaces, APIs, CLI, MCP, and WebMCP without a separate bot surface. Awareness is not authority: discovery never grants permission.

## Canonical technical documentation

- https://s-m-r-t.dev/ — the s-m-r-t application stack: its five layers, the package scope map, and a source-linked evidence table
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/reference/saadl — Software as Agentic Domain Logic and human/agent parity
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/capabilities/agent-legible-applications — manifests, control descriptions, MCP/WebMCP schemas, and bounded runtime awareness
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/capabilities/agent-assisted-forms — stable control identities, validation, staged changes, and confirmation
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/capabilities/webmcp — selected browser tools using the signed-in page session
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/tooling/app-mcp — generated and application MCP for permitted runtime data operations
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/tooling/dev-mcp — read-only development MCP for workspace and installed-package knowledge
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/reference/security — authentication, tenant scope, writable-field policy, and authorization boundaries
- https://s-m-r-t.dev/playground — component and package demonstrations

## Released boundaries

This site documents the installed s-m-r-t release. The framework supports a shared domain model and manifest. It generates REST, CLI, MCP, and selected WebMCP surfaces. Agent-assisted form controls support explain, validate, staged-change, and confirmed-apply flows. Application MCP surfaces include allow-lists and policy checks. These explicit surfaces do not expose every model method or field.

Generated runtime operations still resolve through the application’s principal, tenant scope, field policy, writable-field rules, permissions, and any required confirmation. Development MCP is a separate, read-only workspace plane; it does not access a running application, application data, principals, tenants, or credentials.

## Runtime-environment registry boundary: conditional and unreleased by default

The released development MCP does not connect to a running application or inspect its live ObjectRegistry. A future or application-provided runtime bridge can expose bounded capability metadata after explicit installation, exposure, and discovery. Do not assume that a runtime-environment registry exists. Such a bridge must distinguish observed facts from declared facts. The bridge must not expose application records, credentials, principals, or tenant data. Live data operations remain on the generated and application MCP runtime plane and remain policy-controlled.
